onboarding.title: Before the first analysis
onboarding.intro: Signalyze reads the reviews already shown on the Google Maps page you are looking at. You decide whether a stripped-down copy may be sent to the Signalyze server.
onboarding.sent.title: What is sent
onboarding.sent.body: Star rating, calendar day, review text, the reviewer's public review count, photo count and Local Guide level, plus the place identifier from the URL.
onboarding.neverSent.title: What is never sent
onboarding.neverSent.body: Reviewer names, profile links, avatars, user ids, your Google account, your browsing history.
onboarding.hash: Each reviewer is represented by a one-way hash that changes every day and cannot be linked across places.
onboarding.server: The server keeps only the computed profile per place for 7 days and never stores review text.
onboarding.changeLater: You can change this at any time in Settings.
home.noTab.title: Open a business on Google Maps
home.noTab.body: Signalyze works on Google Maps business pages. Open one, then come back to this panel.
home.noPlace.title: No business selected
home.noPlace.body: Select a business on the map to see its Review Profile.
home.noScript.title: Reload the Google Maps tab
home.noScript.body: The page was opened before Signalyze was installed. Reload it once to connect.
home.cached.title: Result from {date}
home.scope.hint: Loads the reviews at a human pace from the page you are looking at and computes the profile. Nothing runs on its own.
home.scope.windowHint: Google shows review dates approximately ("2 months ago"), so a period is approximate too.
collecting.title: Reading reviews
collecting.hint: The review panel scrolls by itself. Keep the tab open.
result.mandatory: This score is a statistical summary of public review data; it is not a claim about the business or any reviewer.
result.source.window: computed in your browser for this period
result.window.notSorted: Google's Newest order could not be selected; the period was applied to the reviews that were loaded.
result.fallback: The server could not be reached; the analysis ran in your browser.
result.collect.exhausted: Google showed fewer reviews than requested.
result.reading.typical: The measured patterns look like typical businesses.
result.reading.some: Some measurements differ from typical businesses; the list below shows which.
result.reading.many: Many measurements differ clearly from typical businesses; see which ones below.
result.reading.most: Most measurements are far from typical businesses; see which ones below.
result.scale: 0 = every measurement typical, 100 = every measurement at its extreme. One signal can add at most {max} points.
result.contributors.title: What makes up the score
signals.title: Signals
signal.burst_ratio.name: Burst ratio
signal.burst_ratio.short: Share of reviews inside the busiest 14-day window
signal.burst_ratio.why: Review flow at established places is spread out; a large share arriving within two weeks is measurable and rare.
signal.burst_ratio.explain: {peakPercent}% of reviews were posted within one {windowDays}-day window ({start} – {end}).
signal.burst_ratio.plain: {peakPercent}% of the reviews ({peakCount}) were written in the {windowDays} days from {start} to {end}. Spread evenly over {years} years, that window would hold about {expectedPercent}%; the excess is {excessPercent}%.
signal.burst_ratio.baseline: Typical businesses stay below {low}% excess; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.burst_ratio.lookAt: Open the reviews from those dates: an opening, a campaign or a news story may explain the peak.
signal.rating_polarity.name: Rating polarity
signal.rating_polarity.why: Google ratings lean towards 5 stars, so only distributions that almost entirely skip 2 to 4 stars stand out.
signal.rating_polarity.explain: {percent}% of ratings are 5 or 1 stars ({share5}% five-star, {share1}% one-star).
signal.rating_polarity.plain: {percent}% of the ratings are 5 or 1 stars ({share5}% five, {share1}% one); 2, 3 and 4 stars make up {middle}%.
signal.rating_polarity.baseline: Google ratings lean towards 5 stars anyway: typical businesses stay below {low}%; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.rating_polarity.lookAt: Middle ratings (2 to 4 stars) are usually the most detailed; read those first if there are any.
signal.single_review_accounts.name: Single-review accounts
signal.single_review_accounts.short: Reviewers whose public count is 0 or 1
signal.single_review_accounts.why: Most Google reviewers have written more than one review; a large share whose only review is this one differs from that baseline.
signal.single_review_accounts.explain: {percent}% of reviewers with a visible count have no other review ({singles} of {known}).
signal.single_review_accounts.unavailabl: Fewer than {minKnown} reviewers show a review count ({known} found).
signal.single_review_accounts.plain: Of the {known} reviewers whose review count is shown, {singles} ({percent}%) have written no other review.
signal.single_review_accounts.baseline: Typical businesses stay below {low}%; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.single_review_accounts.lookAt: Clicking a reviewer's name shows their other reviews; reviewers with a longer history give you more to compare.
signal.no_photo_short_text.name: No photo, short text
signal.no_photo_short_text.short: Reviews with neither a photo nor a longer text
signal.no_photo_short_text.why: Photos and longer texts take effort; their near-total absence is measurable. Rating-only reviews are common, so only very high shares count.
signal.no_photo_short_text.explain: {percent}% of reviews have no photo and fewer than {chars} characters ({count} reviews).
signal.no_photo_short_text.plain: {percent}% of the reviews ({count}) have no photo and fewer than {chars} characters of text.
signal.no_photo_short_text.baseline: Rating-only reviews are common: typical businesses stay below {low}%; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.no_photo_short_text.lookAt: Reviews with photos and longer texts carry concrete detail; filter by photos to read those first.
signal.text_similarity.name: Text similarity
signal.text_similarity.why: Independently written texts about the same place share some words but very few 3-gram-level fragments, in any language.
signal.text_similarity.explain: Average text overlap {mean} (3-gram Jaccard); {pairPercent}% of pairs are near-duplicates ({highPairs} of {pairs}).
signal.text_similarity.unavailable: Fewer than {minEligible} reviews have at least 20 characters of text ({eligible} found).
signal.text_similarity.plain: The texts overlap by {meanPercent}% on average; {highPairs} of {pairs} text pairs ({pairPercent}%) are nearly identical.
signal.text_similarity.sampledNote: Computed on {sampled} of {eligible} texts, evenly spaced.
signal.text_similarity.baseline: Independently written texts about the same place typically overlap below {meanLow}% ({meanHigh}% and above is extreme); nearly identical pairs stay below {pairLow}% ({pairHigh}% and above is extreme).
signal.text_similarity.lookAt: If several reviews use almost the same sentences, read them side by side.
signal.template_phrases.name: Template phrases
signal.template_phrases.short: Texts that consist mostly of stock phrases
signal.template_phrases.why: Stock phrases occur in everyday reviews too, so only texts that are mostly stock phrases count, and only their share among texts matters.
signal.template_phrases.explain: {percent}% of texts consist mostly of stock phrases ({phraseBased} of {withText}); most frequent: {top}.
signal.template_phrases.unavailable: Fewer than {minWithText} reviews contain text ({withText} found).
signal.template_phrases.plain: {phraseBased} of the {withText} reviews with text ({percent}%) consist mostly of stock phrases; most frequent: {top}.
signal.template_phrases.baseline: Typical businesses stay below {low}%; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.template_phrases.lookAt: Reviews with specifics (what was ordered, who helped, how long it took) tell you more than stock phrases.
signal.rating_text_mismatch.name: Rating and text
signal.rating_text_mismatch.short: Text tone that disagrees with the star rating
signal.rating_text_mismatch.why: Text and stars normally agree. The lexicon does not handle negation or sarcasm, so a baseline of mismatches is expected and does not count.
signal.rating_text_mismatch.explain: {percent}% of scored reviews have a text tone that disagrees with the stars ({mismatches} of {scored}).
signal.rating_text_mismatch.unavailable: Fewer than {minScored} reviews contain words from the tone lexicon ({scored} found).
signal.rating_text_mismatch.plain: In {mismatches} of the {scored} reviews that contain words from the tone lexicon ({percent}%), the tone of the text disagrees with the stars (for example a negative text with 5 stars).
signal.rating_text_mismatch.baseline: Because the lexicon ignores irony and negation, up to {low}% is typical; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.rating_text_mismatch.lookAt: Read the text together with the stars; the star count alone can mislead.
signal.date_entropy.name: Date entropy
signal.date_entropy.short: How evenly reviews are spread over the months
signal.date_entropy.why: Complements the burst ratio at the scale of months; seasonal places have somewhat lower entropy, which the calibration tolerates.
signal.date_entropy.explain: Review dates are spread with {percent}% of the maximum evenness over {months} months; busiest month {busiest} ({busiestPercent}%).
signal.date_entropy.unavailable: The reviews span fewer than {minMonths} months ({months} found).
signal.date_entropy.plain: Over {months} months the reviews reach {percent}% of a perfectly even spread; the busiest month is {busiest} with {busiestPercent}% of them.
signal.date_entropy.baseline: Typical businesses stay above {typicalAbove}%; {extremeBelow}% and below is the extreme end. Seasonal businesses sit a little lower.
signal.date_entropy.lookAt: Check the monthly chart: do the busy months line up with a season or an event?
signal.local_guide_ratio.name: Local Guide share
signal.local_guide_ratio.short: Reviews from Local Guides of level 3 or higher
signal.local_guide_ratio.why: Established Local Guides are a normal part of the reviewer mix at most places; a low share is the unusual direction.
signal.local_guide_ratio.explain: {percent}% of reviews come from Local Guides of level {level} or higher ({established} reviews).
signal.local_guide_ratio.unavailable: The page does not show Local Guide levels.
signal.local_guide_ratio.plain: {percent}% of the reviews ({established}) come from Local Guides at level {level} or higher.
signal.local_guide_ratio.baseline: Established Local Guides are part of the mix at most places: {typicalAtLeast}% and above is typical; 0% is the extreme end.
signal.local_guide_ratio.lookAt: Local Guide profiles are public; their other reviews are a useful comparison.
signal.owner_response_pattern.name: Owner responses
signal.owner_response_pattern.short: How identical the owner's responses are
signal.owner_response_pattern.why: A small, measurable aspect of how the page is managed; many owners reuse one thank-you line, so only near-total repetition counts.
signal.owner_response_pattern.explain: {percent}% of owner responses are identical to another response ({responded} responses, {distinct} distinct).
signal.owner_response_pattern.unavailabl: Fewer than {minResponded} reviews have an owner response ({responded} found).
signal.owner_response_pattern.plain: Of the {responded} owner replies only {distinct} are different; {percent}% repeat another reply word for word.
signal.owner_response_pattern.baseline: Many businesses reuse one thank-you line: up to {low}% repetition is typical; {high}% and above is the extreme end.
signal.owner_response_pattern.lookAt: This signal describes how the page is managed, not the reviewers.

reviewers.title: Reviewers
reviewers.note: Shares are computed over the reviews analysed; “n/a” means the page did not show that information.
state.layout.title: Google's layout changed
state.layout.body: An update is coming. Until then Signalyze shows no numbers rather than risk wrong ones.
state.insufficient.title: Not enough reviews
state.insufficient.body: {count} reviews were found. A score is only computed from {min} reviews on, because smaller samples produce extreme ratios.
state.insufficient.window: {period}: {count} reviews found; a score needs at least {min}. Choose a longer period.
state.error.title: Analysis could not be completed
state.error.body: Try again. If it keeps failing, reload the Google Maps tab.
settings.title: Settings
settings.badge.help: Shows a small Signalyze pill under the business name.
settings.sendToServer: Send data to the Signalyze server
settings.sendToServer.help: Sends the stripped-down review data (no reviewer identifiers) so the profile can be shared through the cache. Off: every analysis runs in your browser.
settings.about: Signalyze makes no claim about the accuracy of any review and no claim about any business or reviewer.
